newsitem.title: CYPRUS: SOMO to renew most 90-day crude contracts - MEES.
newsitem.headline: SOMO to renew most 90-day crude contracts - MEES.

text.p: Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) will renew most of its crude contracts for the next 90-day period of the United Nations oil-for-food deal, the Middle East Econoimc Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

"Our marketing policy for the second 90-day period is basically a continuation of the present one. Most of the 90-day contracts will be renewed," MEES quoted an unnamed but senior SOMO official as saying.
The first renewal date for the oil-for-food deal, which allows Bahgdad to export $1 billion of its crude in this time frame, is March 10.
During the first 90-day period SOMO signed 26 contracts for a total of around 523,000 barrels per day (bpd) out of which 177,000 bpd were for the first 90-day period only, MEES said.
SOMO had also signed contracts for a total of 368,000 bpd for the second 90-day period.

"What is not yet clear is the volume, how much each company will get. They will not necessarily be allocated the same volumes. That will depend on price, how many firms apply and whether the present 90-day lifters want more or less," the SOMO senior official told the Cyprus-based MEES.
"If prices go down and we have additional volume, then we will definitely try to sign up new customers. Otherwise, the present lifters will get priority," the official added.
